o.text: Inherited from Old Anatolian Turkish طات (dat), داد (dad), from Proto-Turkic *tātïg, a derivation from Proto-Turkic *tāt-. Cognate with Turkish tat, Bashkir тат (tat), Kazakh тәтті (tätti, “sweet, palatable”) Gagauz dat etc.
Possibly from Arabic إِمْدَاد (ʔimdād), verbal noun of Arabic أَمَدَّ (ʔamadda).
Borrowed from Arabic جُغْرَافِيَا (juḡrāfiyā), from Ancient Greek γεωγραφία (geōgraphía).
Ultimately from Middle Mongol 馬闌勒 (mǎránlè /⁠maral⁠/, “hind; doe of a red deer”).
